value.body: A private bank probationary officer joins as a trainee officer, completes a training course and then works in branch roles such as customer service, sales, operations and credit. Private sector banks hire them, often through tie-ups with training institutes. A day involves serving customers, meeting sales targets, processing accounts and loans, and following compliance rules.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Any graduate degree; age and score limits vary by bank

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Banks recruit through online tests and interviews, often followed by a paid or bank-sponsored PG diploma or certificate course at a partner institute. Some programmes carry a service bond. Unlike public sector banks, there is no common IBPS exam.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Sales of banking and insurance products

value.title: At a glance
items: Sales targets are a significant part of many private bank roles.
Common next roles: relationship manager, branch operations manager, branch manager.
Check course fees, bond terms and posting policies before joining a programme.
